weighted_loss.note: every population total in weighted.json is a complete-case total over the kept rows; this is what the excluded rows would have added. They carry no CBC, so their anemia burden can be bounded but not measured.

attrition_profile.mcar_note: a difference here rules MCAR out; the absence of one does not rule it in
attrition_profile.note: age sets the WHO cut-off, so non-random loss in age is non-random loss in the label

who_thresholds.note: the flat cut is wrong about the THRESHOLD for far more people than it is wrong about the LABEL: most people are nowhere near either cut-off. Both counts are reported because quoting only the first overstates the damage and quoting only the second understates the error.

pregnancy.flip_definition: guessed, currently anemic, and with hemoglobin at or above the cut-off who_thresholds would assign the same row if it were coded pregnant
pregnancy.no_pregnant_band_note: rows where coding the flag on would not move the cut-off at all, so no flip is possible: girls 12-14, for whom this implementation keeps the 12.0 band. WHO sets no lower age bound on the pregnancy cut-off, so that is an implementation choice, and it is inert here because RIDEXPRG is collected only at ages 20-44.
pregnancy.direction: reported prevalence is an upper bound for this group

integrity.policy: report, do not clean. A plausibility filter would move the denominator of every number in the paper on the basis of the analyst's idea of a normal patient, and in the primary cycle the values it would remove are real extreme phenotypes - two MCVs at 35.4 fL and one WBC at 400 x10^3/uL. The complete-case filter is the only exclusion in this study, and its bias is quantified in attrition_profile.
integrity.adjudication: being outside these bounds does not make a value real, and being inside them does not make it right. The primary cycle's three were checked one at a time; outlying_values names every flagged value with its SEQN so the same can be done for any cycle. 2013-2014's SEQN 77520 (MCHC 69.6 g/dL, RBC 1.67, MCH 74.5) is not a phenotype - it is internally consistent across all three analyser identities and still physically impossible, which is what a unit error looks like. It is retained, because this screen drops nothing, and disclosed here.

provenance_note: seed is dp.SEED, used for the StratifiedKFold shuffle, both forests and the Rao-Wu replicate generator. n_replicates applies to PR-AUC and to the three fit-weight contrasts; every other metric here is a linearised ratio estimate with no resampling.

design.population_represented_note: population_represented is the total for the 12,156 analysed rows only. The 1,616 rows dropped for an incomplete CBC represent a further 26.0 million (8.14% of the merged frame), whose anemia burden is unmeasurable because they have no CBC. Every population count in this file is therefore a lower bound on the frame.

Anemia.se_ratio_note: design_effect and its square root are the inflation of the POPULATION proportion's variance, both SEs taken at the weighted p. se_ratio_vs_conventional_binomial is the different, smaller question a reader actually asks: how much wider the design interval is than the binomial interval a conventional paper puts around its UNWEIGHTED p-hat. Quoting sqrt(design_effect) for that overstates it, because weighting moves the proportion and sqrt(p(1-p)) is not flat between the two values.
Anemia.deff_decomposition_note: design_effect = deff_unequal_weighting x deff_clustering_residual. The first is the Kish factor 1 + CV^2(w) and comes from deliberate oversampling; the second is what the clustering costs. For THIS estimate, attributing the whole design effect to clustering overstates it by 2.42x - read deff_unequal_weighting, not a remembered number from another row.
Anemia.population_note: complete-case: these totals are what the 12,156 analysed rows represent, not the whole NHANES frame. See complete_case_population_excluded in the design block.
Anemia.singleton_strata_note: None: every stratum has at least 2 PSUs, so no variance contribution was dropped.

model_oof.split: 5-fold out-of-fold over all rows; dp.split3 is deliberately not used here

shared_cluster_optimism.mechanism: row-wise folds put all 49 stratum-by-PSU cells in every training fold, so a row is predicted by a model that saw its cluster-mates
shared_cluster_optimism.magnitude_source: ablation.json cluster_holdout, which holds PSUs out instead of rows
shared_cluster_optimism.relative_to_ci_half_width: 0.32x to 1.08x of the design-based 95% half-width for this estimate (0.005399)
shared_cluster_optimism.direction: the accuracy below is optimistic by this much
shared_cluster_optimism.why_not_fixed: a PSU-held-out estimate cannot carry a design-based interval on the full design, which is the point of this block, so the optimism is disclosed rather than removed. Read exceeds_ci_half_width before treating it as small: this key used to end 'the optimism is smaller than the interval', and the worst rung's optimism is about 1.1x this interval's half-width, so that clause was false in the same dict as the number that refutes it

specificity.se_ratio_note: design_effect and its square root are the inflation of the POPULATION proportion's variance, both SEs taken at the weighted p. se_ratio_vs_conventional_binomial is the different, smaller question a reader actually asks: how much wider the design interval is than the binomial interval a conventional paper puts around its UNWEIGHTED p-hat. Quoting sqrt(design_effect) for that overstates it, because weighting moves the proportion and sqrt(p(1-p)) is not flat between the two values.
specificity.deff_decomposition_note: design_effect = deff_unequal_weighting x deff_clustering_residual. The first is the Kish factor 1 + CV^2(w) and comes from deliberate oversampling; the second is what the clustering costs. For THIS estimate, attributing the whole design effect to clustering overstates it by 2.39x - read deff_unequal_weighting, not a remembered number from another row.

significance.correction: Holm step-down over the three contrasts above
significance.note: p_holm is the value every verdict in this block reads. p_value is kept beside it so a reader can see the size of the correction rather than take it on trust.

fit_weight_sensitivity.verdict: Fitting with survey weights changes 1.538% of predictions and moves 1 of 3 population-scale metrics detectably after Holm correction across the three (accuracy -0.0039 (Holm p 0.003)). It does not improve them, so weighting the fit is not a free upgrade: the unweighted fit is reported because it is what the manuscript trained AND because weighting the fit does not help on the population scale.
